front: What is community property under Fam. Code § 760?
back: All property, real or personal, wherever situated, acquired by a married person during the marriage while domiciled in California, unless a statute provides otherwise. Each spouse owns a present, existing and equal one-half interest (§ 751).

front: What are the categories of separate property?
back: Property owned before marriage; property acquired during marriage by gift, bequest, devise or descent; rents, issues and profits of SP (§ 770); earnings and accumulations after the date of separation (§ 771) or after a legal separation judgment (§ 772).

front: Is an inheritance received during marriage CP or SP in California?
back: SP of the heir (§ 770(a)(2)), with its rents and profits, so long as it can be traced. Unlike the PRC default, the will need not designate one spouse.

front: Define quasi-community property (Fam. Code § 125).
back: Property, wherever situated, acquired by either spouse while domiciled elsewhere that would have been CP had the acquiring spouse been domiciled in California, or acquired in exchange for such property.

front: When does a California court apply QCP at dissolution?
back: When both spouses are domiciled in California at dissolution (Marriage of Roesch); QCP is then part of the community estate divided equally (§§ 63, 2550). Constitutional under Addison v. Addison.

front: What does 'community estate' include?
back: Both community property and quasi-community property (Fam. Code § 63).

front: When does the marital economic community begin and end?
back: It begins at marriage and ends at the date of separation (§ 70) or death. Premarital cohabitation creates no CP.

front: What law determines the character of personal property acquired while the couple lived in another state?
back: The law of the acquiring spouse's domicile at acquisition; land follows the situs. CP keeps its character after a move away; California re-characterizes out-of-state acquisitions as QCP only at dissolution or death.

front: Who is a putative spouse and what does that status give?
back: A party to a void or voidable marriage who believed in good faith it was valid. The court divides quasi-marital property (what would have been CP/QCP) equally (Fam. Code § 2251).

front: Is putative-spouse good faith objective or subjective?
back: Subjective: the party's actual honest belief; reasonableness is only evidence (Ceja v. Rudolph & Sletten, 2013).

front: Do registered domestic partners and unmarried cohabitants have CP?
back: Registered domestic partners: yes, same rights as spouses (§ 297.5). Cohabitants: no CP; contract or equitable claims under Marvin v. Marvin.

front: What are the three steps of characterizing an asset?
back: 1) Source and time of acquisition; 2) presumptions (general, title, undue influence); 3) actions of the parties (agreements, transmutation, commingling), then contributions (apportionment, reimbursement), then division.

front: What character do rents and profits take?
back: The character of the property producing them (§ 770(a)(3)), except to the extent community labor produced them, which requires apportionment.

front: A bonus earned during marriage is paid after the date of separation. CP or SP?
back: CP: character follows when it was earned, not when paid.

front: State the general community property presumption.
back: Property acquired during marriage by a spouse domiciled in California is presumed CP; the SP proponent must rebut it, generally by a preponderance, by tracing to an SP source or proving acquisition before marriage, by gift/inheritance or after DOS.

front: CP funds buy an asset titled only in W's name. What is its character?
back: CP, unless there was a valid § 852 transmutation. Evid. Code § 662's title presumption does not apply between spouses where it conflicts with the transmutation statutes (Marriage of Valli, 2014).

front: State the § 2581 joint-title presumption.
back: For division at dissolution or legal separation, property acquired during marriage in joint form is presumed CP, rebuttable only by a clear SP statement in the deed or title document, or a written agreement that it is SP.

front: After § 2581 makes a house CP, how is a spouse's SP down payment protected?
back: § 2640 reimbursement: the traced SP contribution is repaid without interest or appreciation, capped at net value, unless waived in writing.

front: Does § 2581 apply at death?
back: No. It applies only to dissolution and legal separation. In re Brace (2020) makes CP-funded joint tenancy property presumptively CP absent a § 852 writing, but it did not disturb survivorship at death: the surviving joint tenant takes the whole.

front: What is the married woman's pre-1975 presumption?
back: Property acquired by a married woman by written instrument before Jan. 1, 1975 is presumed her SP; if taken with another, she takes as a tenant in common; if taken by 'husband and wife' so described, it is presumed CP (Fam. Code § 803).

front: When does the presumption of undue influence arise between spouses?
back: When an interspousal transaction gives one spouse an advantage. The advantaged spouse must prove the other acted freely, voluntarily, with full knowledge and complete understanding (§ 721; Marriage of Haines).

front: Does the § 721 undue-influence presumption apply to premarital agreements?
back: No. Prospective spouses are not yet fiduciaries (Marriage of Bonds); § 1615 governs enforceability instead.

front: W's mother deeds a house 'to H and W as joint tenants.' Character at dissolution?
back: Gift to both spouses; because title was taken in joint form during marriage, § 2581 presumes CP at dissolution (no SP statement in the deed). Each spouse ends up with half either way; no § 2640 claim because neither contributed SP.

front: What are the formation requirements for a premarital agreement?
back: In writing and signed by both parties; enforceable without consideration (§ 1611); effective on marriage (§ 1613); amend or revoke after marriage only by signed writing (§ 1614).

front: List the § 1615(c) voluntariness requirements.
back: 1) Independent counsel, or separate written waiver after advice (advice ≥ 7 days before signing); 2) ≥ 7 calendar days between first receiving the final agreement and signing; 3) if unrepresented, written explanation in a language the party understands + signed acknowledgment; 4) no duress, fraud, undue influence or incapacity; 5) other factors.

front: When is a premarital agreement unenforceable for unconscionability?
back: If unconscionable when executed AND the challenger got no fair disclosure, did not waive disclosure in writing, and had no adequate knowledge (§ 1615(a)(2)). Unconscionability is a question of law.

front: When is a premarital spousal-support waiver unenforceable?
back: If the party against whom it is enforced lacked independent counsel at signing, or the provision is unconscionable at the time of enforcement (§ 1612(c)).

front: Can a premarital agreement limit child support?
back: No; a child's right to support may not be adversely affected (§ 1612(b)).

front: What are the three kinds of transmutation (§ 850)?
back: CP to SP of either spouse; SP of either spouse to CP; SP of one spouse to SP of the other.

front: What formalities does § 852(a) require for a transmutation?
back: A writing containing an express declaration, made, joined in, consented to or accepted by the spouse whose interest is adversely affected (for transmutations on or after Jan. 1, 1985).

front: Does part performance save an oral transmutation?
back: No (Marriage of Benson, 2005).

front: What is the 'express declaration' test?
back: The writing itself must expressly state that the character or ownership of the property is being changed; extrinsic evidence cannot supply it (Estate of MacDonald, 1990).

front: Does a spouse's signed consent to the other's IRA beneficiary designation transmute her CP interest?
back: No; it lacks an express declaration of a change of ownership (Estate of MacDonald). Under Prob. Code § 5022 consent is not a transmutation unless it meets § 852.

front: Did a broker instruction to 'transfer' stock into W's name transmute it?
back: No (Marriage of Barneson, 1999): no express statement of a change in ownership.

front: What does the § 852(c) personal-gift exception cover?
back: Interspousal gifts of clothing, wearing apparel, jewelry or other tangible personal articles used solely or principally by the donee and not substantial in value given the circumstances of the marriage; no writing needed.

front: Can a car or boat given by one spouse to the other fall under § 852(c)?
back: Generally no: not a personal article of the clothing/jewelry type and usually substantial in value; a writing is needed.

front: How are pre-1985 transmutations proved?
back: § 852 does not apply before Jan. 1, 1985; they could be oral or inferred from conduct (§ 852(e)).

front: A transmutation deed satisfies § 852 and benefits H. Anything else to analyze?
back: Yes: presumption of undue influence (§ 721; Haines); H must prove W acted freely with full understanding. Also § 2640 reimbursement if SP became CP.

front: Is a recorded transmutation of real property needed against third parties?
back: Yes; it is not effective against third parties without notice unless recorded (§ 852(b)); transmutations are subject to fraudulent-transfer law (§ 851).

front: Can spouses alter non-property legal relations by contract?
back: No; only property relations (Fam. Code § 1620). Marital agreements are reviewed under the fiduciary duty (§ 721).

front: What is the effect of commingling SP and CP?
back: Character does not change by itself, but if SP cannot be traced, the commingled mass is CP; the SP claimant must trace (See v. See).

front: State the direct-tracing method.
back: Show with adequate records that SP funds were available in the account when the purchase was made and that the spouse intended to use SP funds (Marriage of Mix, 1975).

front: State the exhaustion method.
back: Show that, at the time of purchase, all CP in the account had been exhausted by family expenses, so the purchase was necessarily made with SP (See v. See, 1966).

front: What is the family expense presumption?
back: Family living expenses are presumed paid from CP when available; SP used for family expenses is presumed a gift with no reimbursement (See v. See).

front: Is total recapitulation enough to trace?
back: No. Showing that total SP deposits exceeded SP withdrawals over the marriage does not trace a particular purchase (See v. See).

front: When must growth in an SP business be apportioned?
back: When more-than-minimal community labor during marriage contributed to the increase; growth from capital or market alone stays SP.

front: State the Pereira method.
back: SP receives the capital at marriage plus a fair rate of return (often the legal rate, simple interest) for the years of marriage; the rest of the value is CP. Used when growth is due to the spouse's personal efforts.

front: What rate of return did Beam v. Bank of America accept under Pereira?
back: The legal rate (7%) where no better evidence was offered; no fixed rate is required and a higher rate may be justified.

front: State the Van Camp method.
back: CP receives the reasonable value of the spouse's services during marriage less the salary or family expenses already drawn; the rest is SP. Used when growth is due to the capital or market conditions.

front: How does a court choose between Pereira and Van Camp?
back: Whichever achieves substantial justice: Pereira for effort-driven growth, Van Camp for capital-driven growth; neither is mandatory (Beam; Dekker). On the essay apply both.

front: State the Moore formula for community payments on SP real property.
back: CP% = CP principal reduction ÷ purchase price. CP share = CP principal paid + (CP% × appreciation during marriage). SP = equity − CP share. Interest, taxes and insurance excluded.

front: What did Marriage of Marsden add to Moore?
back: Appreciation before marriage belongs entirely to the SP owner; only appreciation during marriage is shared pro rata.

front: CP funds remodel W's premarital house. Remedy?
back: Community reimbursement (cost or value added); consent to the spending is not a gift (Marriage of Allen, 2002).

front: Do CP payments of mortgage interest and property taxes on SP create a community interest?
back: No; they are treated as the cost of the community's use of the property (Moore).

front: Inherited index fund doubles with minimal effort. Character of the gain?
back: SP; passive growth and income of SP remain SP.

front: State § 2640(b).
back: At dissolution a party is reimbursed for SP contributions (down payments, improvements, principal reduction; not interest, taxes, insurance, maintenance) to acquisition of CP, traced to SP, unless waived in writing; no interest or appreciation; capped at net value.

front: What does § 2640(c) add?
back: SP contributions to the acquisition of the other spouse's SP during marriage are reimbursed unless there was a written transmutation or a written waiver.

front: What did Marriage of Lucas hold and what replaced it?
back: SP contributions to jointly titled property were presumed a gift absent agreement; replaced by §§ 2581 and 2640 (effective 1984), with limits on retroactivity.

front: W transmutes her SP house into joint tenancy. Can she still get § 2640 reimbursement?
back: Likely yes, unless there is an express written waiver or a writing with that effect; donative intent alone does not bar it (Marriage of Carpenter). The other spouse argues the deed has the effect of a waiver.

front: Is a professional degree community property?
back: No (Marriage of Sullivan). The community is reimbursed under § 2641, the exclusive remedy.

front: State the § 2641 reimbursement rule.
back: Community is reimbursed for community contributions to a party's education or training that substantially enhance earning capacity, with interest at the legal rate from the end of each calendar year of payment; educational loans are assigned to that party.

front: What are the § 2641 ten-year presumptions?
back: Community presumed NOT to have substantially benefited from contributions made less than 10 years before the proceeding, and presumed to HAVE benefited from contributions made more than 10 years before.

front: Are unvested pension rights CP?
back: Yes, to the extent earned by employment during marriage before DOS (Marriage of Brown, 1976).

front: State the time rule for pensions.
back: Community fraction = months of service during marriage before DOS ÷ total months of service; that fraction of each payment is CP.

front: What is the Gillmore election?
back: When the employee spouse is eligible to retire, the non-employee spouse may elect to receive his or her community share immediately (Marriage of Gillmore, 1981).

front: How are pensions divided at dissolution?
back: Cash-out of present value with offsetting assets, or in-kind division of each payment (reserved jurisdiction), often through a QDRO; § 2610 requires orders protecting each party's full share.

front: How are disability benefits characterized?
back: By what they replace: replacement of post-DOS earnings is SP; substitute for retirement earned during marriage is CP (Stenquist; Saslow).

front: How is severance pay characterized?
back: By what it compensates: services during marriage → CP; replacement of post-DOS earnings → SP.

front: Hug vs. Nelson formulas for stock options?
back: Hug (options rewarding past services): start of employment → DOS ÷ start of employment → exercisable date. Nelson (future services): grant → DOS ÷ grant → exercisable date. Trial court discretion.

front: How is term life insurance characterized?
back: Generally by the source of the premium for the final term in which the insured died (Burwell); renewal after DOS with SP → SP. Whole life is apportioned by premiums. Title alone does not control (Valli).

front: Is goodwill of a professional practice CP?
back: Yes, to the extent developed during marriage; valuation excludes post-DOS efforts (Golden; Foster; Lopez).

front: When are personal-injury damages CP?
back: When the cause of action arose during marriage (§ 780). SP if it arose after a dissolution/legal-separation judgment, while living separate, or against the other spouse (§ 781), or before marriage.

front: W wins the lottery with a ticket bought from CP and hides it. Result?
back: Winnings are CP; fraudulent concealment → 100% to H under § 1101(h) (Marriage of Rossi).

front: How are credit acquisitions characterized?
back: Presumptively CP; loan proceeds are SP only if the lender intended to and did rely primarily (traditionally solely) on the borrower's SP (Gudelj; Grinius).

front: H forges W's signature on a deed of trust on the CP house. Consequences?
back: No joinder → encumbrance voidable/ineffective as to W (§ 1102); breach of fiduciary duty (§§ 721, 1100(e)) with § 1101 remedies; community estate still liable for H's marital debt (§ 910); W's SP not liable (§ 913).

front: Which estates get reimbursed, and which do not?
back: Reimbursed: SP→CP acquisition (§ 2640(b)); SP→other's SP (§ 2640(c)); CP→education (§ 2641); CP→SP improvements; post-DOS SP→community debts (Epstein); statutory debt payments (§ 920). Not reimbursed: SP→family expenses (See).

front: When does a right of reimbursement for paying a debt exist?
back: As the debt statutes provide (§ 920), e.g., §§ 914, 915, 916; measured by value when the right arises; exercise by the earlier of 3 years after actual knowledge or the division/death proceeding; express written waiver bars it.

front: CP paid H's child support from a prior marriage while his SP income was available. Remedy?
back: Community reimbursement from H under § 915 (support obligation not arising from the marriage is treated as a premarital debt).

front: Who manages community personal property?
back: Either spouse, with the same absolute power of disposition (other than by will) as over SP (§ 1100(a)), subject to statutory limits and the fiduciary duty.

front: What does the spousal fiduciary duty require?
back: Highest good faith and fair dealing; no unfair advantage; full disclosure of the existence, character and value of assets and debts; equal access to information; accounting for benefits; lasts until property is divided (§§ 721, 1100(e)).

front: Can a spouse give away CP personal property alone?
back: No; a gift or transfer for less than fair value needs the other's written consent (§ 1100(b)). The gift is voidable: entirely during the donor's life, one-half after death (Spreckels; Fields).

front: What household items need written consent to sell or encumber?
back: Family dwelling personal property, furniture, furnishings or fittings of the home, and the clothing of the other spouse or minor children (§ 1100(c)).

front: What rule governs a community business managed by one spouse?
back: The managing spouse has primary management and may act alone, but must give prior written notice before disposing of all or substantially all of the business's personal property (§ 1100(d)).

front: What does § 1102 require for community real property?
back: Both spouses must join in any sale, conveyance, encumbrance, or lease longer than one year. A sole transfer is voidable; BFP without knowledge of the marriage is protected where title is in one spouse's name; sue within one year of recording.

front: What remedies does § 1101 give for breach of fiduciary duty?
back: Accounting; adding the claimant's name to title; 50% of any asset undisclosed or transferred in breach plus fees and costs; 100% where the breach involves oppression, fraud or malice (Civ. Code § 3294).

front: What is the limitations period for a § 1101 claim?
back: Generally three years from the claimant's actual knowledge of the transaction; it can also be raised in a dissolution, legal separation or death proceeding as the statute provides.

front: Can a spouse sell SP without the other's consent?
back: Yes (§ 770(b)), subject to the fiduciary duty in interspousal transactions and any community interest created by community labor or funds.

front: Define the date of separation under § 70.
back: The date of a complete and final break, shown by both (1) a spouse's expression to the other of the intent to end the marriage and (2) conduct consistent with that intent; all relevant evidence considered.

front: Can spouses separate while living in the same house?
back: Yes. § 70 (eff. 2017) abrogated Marriage of Davis (2015), which had required separate residences.

front: What is the character of earnings after the date of separation?
back: SP of the earning spouse, including accumulations and earnings of minor children in that spouse's custody (§ 771).

front: A community business grows between DOS and trial because of H's work. Who gets the growth?
back: Apportion: return on community capital and passive growth → CP; return on H's post-DOS labor → H's SP (Marriage of Imperato).

front: What is an Epstein credit?
back: Reimbursement to a spouse who used SP (post-DOS earnings) to pay a community obligation after separation and before trial, unless the payment was a gift, support, under a no-reimbursement agreement, or offset by exclusive use.

front: What is a Watts charge?
back: A charge, payable to the community, for one spouse's exclusive post-separation use of a community asset (usually the home), at its reasonable value, in the court's discretion.

front: How is the community estate divided at dissolution?
back: Equally, unless the parties agree in writing or stipulate in open court (§ 2550); valued near trial (§ 2552); in kind or with offsetting assets; SP confirmed to its owner.

front: What is the misappropriation remedy at division?
back: The court may award from a party's share, or offset, any sum that party deliberately misappropriated to the exclusion of the other's community interest (§ 2602).

front: What are the consequences of failing to disclose a community asset in dissolution?
back: 50% (or 100% with fraud) of the asset under § 1101(g)–(h); mandatory monetary sanctions unless justified (§ 2107); § 271 fees; later division of omitted assets (§ 2556); set-aside (§ 2122).

front: How are community personal-injury damages divided at dissolution?
back: Assigned to the injured spouse unless justice requires otherwise, considering needs, economic condition and time elapsed; even then at least one-half to the injured spouse; commingled damages are divided like other CP (§ 2603).

front: H negligently injures W. Character of her recovery and how is it paid?
back: W's SP (§ 781(c)); CP may not be used to pay until H's non-exempt SP is exhausted, unless W consents in writing after the injury; insurance indemnity unaffected (§ 782).

front: How are educational loans allocated at dissolution?
back: Assigned to the spouse who received the education, not divided as community debt (§§ 2627, 2641(b)(2)), subject to § 2641(c) adjustments.

front: How are tort liabilities not incurred for the community's benefit allocated at dissolution?
back: To the spouse whose act or omission gave rise to them, without offset (§ 2627 with § 1000(b)(2)).

front: What if community debts exceed community assets?
back: The excess is assigned as the court deems just and equitable, considering factors such as relative ability to pay (§ 2622(b)).

front: How does a California court divide out-of-state real property?
back: If possible, without changing title (award it to one spouse and offset); otherwise order conveyances or award the money value (§ 2660).

front: Which property is liable for a spouse's debts during marriage?
back: The entire community estate (CP and QCP) for debts either spouse incurred before or during marriage before DOS (§§ 910, 912); the debtor's SP (§ 913(a)); not the non-debtor's SP except for necessaries (§§ 913(b), 914).

front: Can a creditor of H's premarital debt reach W's salary?
back: Not if W's earnings are kept in a deposit account H cannot draw on and are not commingled (§ 911); otherwise the community estate is liable (§ 910).

front: Is the non-debtor spouse's SP liable for the other spouse's debts?
back: No (§ 913(b)), except for necessaries (§ 914); joining in an encumbrance does not expose the joining spouse's SP.

front: When is a spouse personally liable for the other's necessaries?
back: For necessaries of life of the spouse before DOS, and for common necessaries while living separately (§ 914); SP may be applied, with reimbursement if CP or the other's SP was available.

front: How is a spouse's tort liability satisfied?
back: If the tort occurred during an activity for the community's benefit: CP first, then the tortfeasor's SP. Otherwise: the tortfeasor's SP first, then CP (§ 1000). The other spouse's SP is not liable.

front: How are debts allocated at dissolution?
back: Premarital → incurring spouse (§ 2621); marital before DOS → divided equally (§ 2622); post-DOS → incurring spouse unless common necessaries, allocated by need and ability (§ 2623); after judgment → incurring spouse (§ 2624).

front: After division, can a creditor of H reach property awarded to W?
back: Only if the debt was assigned to W in the division, or it is W's own debt; property received follows its owner's own debts (§ 916).

front: What happens to CP at a spouse's death?
back: One-half belongs to the survivor; the other half to the decedent, who may dispose of it by will (Prob. Code §§ 100, 6101). Each spouse owns half of each CP item.

front: What can a married decedent dispose of by will?
back: His or her SP, one-half of the CP and one-half of his or her own QCP (Prob. Code § 6101).

front: What is QCP at death, and what happens to it?
back: Personal property wherever situated and California real property acquired while domiciled elsewhere that would have been CP (Prob. Code § 66). One-half of the DECEDENT'S QCP belongs to the survivor (§ 101); the survivor's own QCP is not split.

front: Is a farm in State X QCP when the spouse dies domiciled in California?
back: No. At death QCP includes only California real property (Prob. Code § 66); State X law governs the farm.

front: State the elements of QCP recapture (Prob. Code § 102).
back: Decedent domiciled in CA; transferred QCP to a non-spouse without substantial consideration and without the survivor's written consent or joinder; decedent retained possession/income, a power to revoke or invade, or held it with right of survivorship → transferee restores one-half to the estate, for the survivor; insurance, annuities and pensions excluded (§ 102(b)).

front: What does a surviving spouse take by intestacy?
back: All CP (decedent's half), the decedent's half of QCP, and of SP: all if no issue, parent, sibling or sibling's issue; one-half if one child (or issue of one) or no issue but parents or their issue; one-third if more children (Prob. Code § 6401).

front: When must a surviving spouse elect?
back: When the will purports to dispose of the survivor's half of CP and also gives the survivor benefits: take under the will or keep the CP half and forgo the will's gifts.

front: H names his brother beneficiary of a CP-funded policy without W's written consent. Result?
back: The transfer does not take effect against W's half; the court may set it aside to that extent (Prob. Code §§ 5020, 5021).

front: What does an omitted spouse receive?
back: The decedent's half of CP, half of the decedent's QCP, and an intestate share of SP not exceeding one-half (Prob. Code § 21610), unless a § 21611 exception applies.

front: What is CP with right of survivorship?
back: A form of holding (Civ. Code § 682.1) that is CP for all purposes but passes to the survivor at death without administration.

front: After the donor spouse dies, how much of an unconsented CP gift can the survivor recover?
back: One-half (the survivor's share); the decedent could have given away his own half (Fields v. Michael).

front: Can a California court divide Social Security benefits or offset them?
back: No. Federal law bars assignment (42 U.S.C. § 407(a)); courts may not divide them or award offsetting property.

front: What did McCarty, USFSPA, Mansell and Howell decide about military retired pay?
back: McCarty: not divisible; USFSPA (10 U.S.C. § 1408): states may divide disposable retired pay; Mansell: pay waived for VA disability not divisible; Howell (2017): no indemnification order for a post-divorce waiver.

front: How does ERISA limit community property law?
back: Plan benefits can be divided only by QDRO (29 U.S.C. § 1056(d)); ERISA preempts a nonparticipant spouse's bequest of pension interests (Boggs) and revocation-on-divorce statutes as to plan designations (Egelhoff).

front: Which federal designations override CP claims?
back: NSLI (Wissner), SGLI (Ridgway), FEGLI (Hillman v. Maretta), and U.S. savings bonds with survivorship (Free v. Bland), subject to the Yiatchos fraud exception.

front: What is the opening paragraph of every CP essay?
back: California is a CP state; property acquired during marriage while domiciled in California is presumed CP (§ 760); property before marriage, after separation, or by gift/inheritance is SP (§ 770); character depends on source, time and actions of the parties; equal division at dissolution (§ 2550).

front: PRC bridge: how does California treat a PI award compared with PRC law (approx.)?
back: PRC: the injured spouse's personal property. California: CP if the claim arose during marriage (§ 780) but assigned to the injured spouse at dissolution (§ 2603), at least half.
